public_rationale: The OECD reports exactly this rounded share for global venture investment in AI firms during 2025. Its published totals also reproduce 61% when divided and rounded.
limitations: The result follows OECD/Preqin coverage and its broad classification of AI firms.
The OECD cautions that historical deal additions and methodological revisions can change estimates.
This does not mean 61% went specifically to generative AI.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: 61% of venture capital funding went to AI in 2025.

statement.excerpt: Everything is about creating the signs that your company is part of the big thing that will supposedly lift every Silicon Valley valuation — after all, 61% of venture capital funding went to AI in 2025 — to the point that it isn’t really clear what anything means or what anybody is doing.

our_interpretation: The unqualified funding share means global investment value, not deal count or US-only funding.
AI includes AI firms broadly, not just generative-AI model developers.
The percentage is rounded to the nearest whole percentage point.
This is an aggregate investment statistic, not a particular company's financial metric; metric_scope is therefore null.
criteria.support_condition: A credible global VC dataset places AI firms' share of 2025 investment value at approximately 61%, using a disclosed classification.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable global data using the same investment and AI definitions establish a materially different share, beyond rounding.
